summary:
An opinion piece from Leukaemia Care (published via Workplace Insight) arguing that corporate charity partnership selection policies are too category-driven and should be judged on impact instead. The author notes that because Leukaemia Care is not exclusively a children's charity, its substantial work with children and young people affected by blood cancer is often overlooked by prospective corporate partners whose policies favour children-only organisations.

The article uses CAR-T (chimeric antigen receptor T cell) therapy support as evidence. In 2025 to 26, 63.4% of applications to the charity's CAR-T support service were from people aged 18 or under, with an average age of nine. Families travelled an average of 113 miles from home to the nearest hospital offering the treatment, with Great Ormond Street, Great North Children's Hospital and Royal Manchester Children's Hospital named as the three NHS paediatric CAR-T centres. Through a partnership with Dalata Hotel Group, the charity provides accommodation: 13 of 64 applicants aged up to 18 used the hotel service, totalling 254 nights, with some stays running to 31 nights.

The piece references the Government's National Cancer Plan for England, published February 2026, which commits up to 10 million pounds a year from 2027 to help children and young people with cancer meet travel costs, citing the 2024 Under-16 Cancer Patient Experience Survey finding that 37.6% of respondents took over an hour to reach their child's main treatment hospital.

The closing argument targets CSR, ESG, sustainability and HR leaders: corporate partners can contribute more than money by matching core capabilities to beneficiary needs, for example retailers offering supply chain and distribution, hospitality firms offering accommodation, meals or meeting space, and employers offering professional expertise or paid volunteering time. Partnerships should be measured by sustained change, not one-off campaign metrics, and employees should be engaged in understanding impact rather than only fundraising.
